title: Priority basket: Positive-ink invoice
summary: Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.
descriptionMd:
A heap-shaped basket keeps the smallest numbered service ticket ready at its opening. Alma prepares an invoice that accepts only positive ink adjustments. Zero and negative derived readings stay off the invoice.

Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates.

Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.

Implement priorityBasketPositiveInkInvoice(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Binary heaps. Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with binary heaps. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [-3,0,7,7,12]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 26.
The derived sequence is [-2,4,4,4]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 12.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 0.
